name: Censer Smoke Manual (Lô Yên Quyết)
rank: sold on pill-market stalls; any alchemist with a censer
concept: A stall manual on how to vent a censer so that what burns in it goes out at a foe. Every alchemist who fights through smoke keeps a copy.
lore: Copied and recopied on the pill markets; the oldest copies are said to be pages torn from the Purple Smoke Furnace Canon.

name: Golden Valley Ledger Canon (Kim Cốc Trướng Kinh)
rank: four copies sold after Kim Cốc Thành fell in 1003
concept: Kim Cốc Viên's main counting-house method: every blow traded enters the ledger, and debt accrued in Earth stacks collects in full.
lore: Kim Cốc Viên pledged its manuals to Quản Doanh Hư in 1002; one copy passed to the Từ house of Thiên Quyền Thị while Quản Phục Thu keeps the original.

name: Second Spring Needle Art (Hồi Xuân Châm Pháp)
rank: clinic needle manual of Hạnh Hoa Thị
concept: Giả Hồi Xuân's apricot-clinic needle method: draws poisons and curses out along the meridian needle and mends deepest at low health.
lore: Taught free at Hạnh Hoa Thị to anyone who will tend a patient for a season.

name: Loom of Letters Array Canon (Văn Cơ Trận Kinh)
rank: portable array manual sold by commission
concept: Vệ Văn Cơ's reworked star-script array canon: portable grid figures relayed in half the time and walked forward under a carried ward.
lore: Cut out of Củng Tinh Quán's armillary craft after Vệ Văn Cơ left the abbey in 1100.

name: Buried Vault Coin Canon (Mai Khố Tiền Kinh)
rank: private vault canon of Kim Vạn Lý
concept: Coin caches tucked behind an Earth-buried body ward: every third toss empties a cache for a second heavy strike while gold buys time behind the shield.
lore: Pieced together over three centuries from western counting-house manuals and caravan guard exercises.

name: Bronze Sounding Canon (Thính Kim Khấu Điển)
rank: appraiser's bronze-testing manual of Thiều Âm Thị
concept: An antique appraiser's Metal-Earth method: tap once to hear the hairline crack in vessel or foe, then strike straight through the fault.
lore: Written for tomb-bell and bronze buyers of Thiều Âm Thị to tell true casting from patched ore.

name: Market Scale Breath (Thị Xứng Công)
rank: common earth-root breathing primer of market towns
concept: A plain Earth breathing primer passed among storekeepers, sugar-boilers, and caravan clerks for steady nerves and heavy palms.
lore: Sold by weight alongside abacus manuals at western market stalls.

name: River Road Breath (Giang Lộ Công)
rank: water-root breathing method of ferrymen and river peddlers
concept: A gentle Water cultivation breath learned on ferries and dockhouses: keeps wind and recovery even across long river voyages.
lore: Passed from boatmaster to deckhand between Yên Ba and Tinh Hán.
